title: URL Manipulation & Video OSINT
description: Deep dive into video investigation techniques, URL parameter manipulation, privacy wrappers, metadata extraction, Geospatial Intelligence (GeoINT), CLI comment scraping, JSON parsing with jq, dark web TOR stream scraping, stream reverse engineering, and AI acoustic forensics.

sections.title: URL Anatomy & Parameter Manipulation
sections.description: URL manipulation is a foundational OSINT technique. Websites use URL parameters to identify content, pass session data, and specify endpoints. Understanding these parameters allows investigators to navigate directly to specific resources, bypass UI restrictions, or extract raw identifiers.
topics: Domain vs Path vs Query String — understanding URL components
Query parameters — identified by '?' and separated by '&'
Extracting unique identifiers (e.g., Video ID 'v=OcXfMo-zuHc') for cross-platform research
Session tracking & footprints — how cookies, IP addresses, and logged-in states affect results
Unauthenticated research — why personal user sessions introduce bias and risk identity leaks

commands.description: Standard YouTube URL. '/watch' is the endpoint, 'v=' is the query parameter, and 'OcXfMo-zuHc' is the unique video ID.
Isolate the video ID parameter to pass into specialized OSINT tools and third-party wrappers.
Direct URL manipulation to access the highest-resolution thumbnail image without opening the video player.

sections.title: Privacy Wrappers & Alternative Interfaces
sections.description: Direct interaction with major platforms exposes browser cookies, session identifiers, and IP addresses. OSINT investigators use alternative web wrappers and privacy frontends to inspect content while minimizing direct session tracking.
sections.note: Third-party wrappers route requests through alternative infrastructure, reducing direct tracking by original platforms. However, wrapper services themselves log IP requests, so use them as privacy tools, not absolute anonymity guarantees.

tools.name: nsfwyoutube.com
tools.description: Third-party web wrapper interface for viewing YouTube videos by modifying domain prefix in the URL.

tools.name: Invidious (yewtu.be)
tools.description: Open-source privacy-focused YouTube frontend with no ads, tracking, or JS bloat.

tools.name: Piped
tools.description: Modern open-source YouTube alternative focusing on privacy, fast load times, and custom instances.

commands.description: Replace 'youtube.com' with 'nsfwyoutube.com' in the URL to inspect content via wrapper.
Load video via Invidious instance to prevent Google session tracking and cookie assignment.

sections.title: YouTube Metadata & Channel Analysis
sections.description: Video pages contain rich metadata beyond what is visible in the standard interface. Extracted metadata provides crucial investigative leads including exact upload timestamps, tags, category IDs, thumbnail links, and uploader channel metrics.

tools.name: MattW YouTube Metadata Viewer
tools.description: Comprehensive online tool for extracting complete structured metadata from YouTube videos, channels, and playlists.

tools.name: yt-dlp
tools.description: Feature-rich CLI tool to extract raw JSON metadata, stream details, and transcripts directly from video URLs.

commands.description: Open MattW Metadata Viewer in browser and enter target YouTube video URL or ID.
Dump complete raw JSON metadata for a video into a local file for offline analysis.

commands.cmd: cat video_metadata.json | jq '{title: .title, upload_date: .upload_date, uploader: .uploader, tags: .tags}'
commands.description: Parse key metadata fields (title, upload date, uploader, tags) from raw yt-dlp JSON dump.

sections.title: Geospatial Intelligence (GeoINT) on Video
sections.description: GeoINT involves connecting digital video evidence to physical real-world locations. By combining geographic location coordinates with relevant search keywords, investigators can identify video footage recorded around protests, incidents, or crime scenes.
sections.note: Location coordinates returned by tools must be verified against actual video content. Geotags can be set manually by uploaders or assigned by platform heuristics.
topics: Location + Keyword search strategy (e.g. City: Delhi, Keyword: protest)
Mapping video search results visually across geographical regions
Extracting raw coordinates, channel IDs, upload times, and location tags
Cross-verification methodology: Matching satellite imagery, street signs, building architecture, and sun angles

tools.name: MattW YouTube Geofind
tools.description: Search YouTube videos by geographic location, custom radius, and search keywords with interactive map plotting.

tools.name: SunCalc
tools.description: Calculate sun position, shadows, and light angles for precise date/time/location verification.

tools.name: Google Earth Pro
tools.description: Desktop GIS application providing 3D historical satellite imagery and elevation profiles.

commands.description: Open YouTube Geofind. Enter target city (e.g. Delhi) and keyword (e.g. protest) to map location-tagged videos.
Open Google Street View directly at target coordinates for visual ground verification.

sections.title: Downloading YouTube Comments via CLI
sections.description: Comment sections often hold critical context, eyewitness reports, timestamps, user leads, and links. Using CLI comment downloaders enables rapid bulk extraction without manual scrolling or API key limitations.

tools.name: youtube-comment-downloader
tools.description: Fast command-line tool to scrape all comments and replies from YouTube videos into structured JSON format.

commands.description: Install youtube-comment-downloader CLI package.
Download all video comments and save structured results to output.json file.
Limit comment collection to 500 entries for faster analysis.

sections.title: Processing & Parsing JSON Data with jq
sections.description: Data collection is distinct from data analysis. Raw JSON files can be cluttered and noisy. Using command-line JSON processors like 'jq' allows investigators to extract clean, formatted fields (Author, Timestamp, Comment Text) and pivot into further leads.
sections.note: A single comment does not provide final proof. Treat comment signatures as leads to pivot across social platforms: Username → Profile → Other Platforms → Additional Evidence.

tools.name: jq
tools.description: Lightweight and flexible command-line JSON processor for filtering, transforming, and parsing data.

commands.description: Display raw JSON comment data in terminal output.
Parse raw JSON comments into clean human-readable 'Author | Time | Text' format.
Filter comments containing a specific target keyword (case-insensitive).

commands.cmd: jq -r '.author' output.json | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 10
commands.description: Analyze top 10 most frequent commenters across the dataset.

sections.title: Dark Web & Onion Video Investigation
sections.description: Advanced techniques for investigating hidden video services on the TOR network (.onion sites). Routing tools through SOCKS5 proxies prevents IP leakage and allows safe extraction of unindexed video metadata.
sections.note: Always maintain strict operational security (OPSEC) when investigating hidden services. Use isolated virtual environments and route all network traffic through dedicated TOR daemons.
topics: SOCKS5 proxy configuration via local TOR SOCKS port (127.0.0.1:9050)
Scraping video streams and raw files from .onion hidden service mirrors
Investigating TOR video gateways, stream servers, and hidden forums
Preventing direct IP exposure during deep web media analysis

tools.name: TOR Network Proxy
tools.description: SOCKS5 network proxy for routing investigation requests through the TOR onion router.

tools.name: Ahmia Search Engine
tools.description: Search index for finding content and hidden services on the TOR network.

commands.description: Download a video file from a .onion hidden service via local TOR SOCKS5 proxy.
Extract stream metadata from a hidden service video URL using yt-dlp over SOCKS5 proxy.

sections.title: Archived & Deleted Video Recovery
sections.description: When target videos are deleted or set to private, historical internet archives contain cached metadata, snapshots, index tags, thumbnail images, and transcripts.

commands.description: Query Wayback Machine CDX API for all archived snapshots of a specific video URL.

sections.title: Reverse Engineering HLS & DASH Streams
sections.description: Modern video portals use HTTP Live Streaming (HLS `.m3u8`) and Dynamic Adaptive Streaming (DASH `.mpd`) to deliver segmented video streams. Reverse engineering network requests allows downloading raw unencrypted media feeds.

tools.name: Streamlink
tools.description: Command-line utility that extracts video streams from various services and redirects them to custom players or files.

commands.description: Capture live HLS video stream directly into an MP4 file using Streamlink.
Download and reassemble segmented HLS .m3u8 video chunks into a single MP4 video file.

sections.title: Live Stream & API Endpoint Forensics
sections.description: Different web platforms expose specialized backend API endpoints during live video streaming. Analyzing these public API endpoints provides access to raw broadcast tokens, metadata, stream parameters, and host account details.
